[118] Recommendation from the Ministry of Defense 18 September 2015, approved by the Council of State on the same day. (Government Solberg

[119] In the introductory part Main goals and priorities In order to be a relevant security policy tool, the Armed Forces must be further developed in line with geopolitical and technological developments

[120] There have been extensive security policy changes since the current long-term plan for the defense sector was adopted by the Storting in

[121] Since then, Norway has gradually entered a more demanding and complex security policy situation

[122] In addition to the challenges stemming from Norway's strategic location and increased international attention to the northern regions, we see more interstate conflicts closer to our areas of interest

[123] Asymmetric threats from non-governmental organizations are still part of the threat picture Norway faces

[124] The security policy situation is characterized by increased unpredictability and uncertainty linked to Russian intentions in our immediate areas

[125] Russia pursues a more aggressive foreign policy

[126] Russia has developed a significantly increased military capability, and has shown a willingness to violate international law and use military force to advance its interests

[127] Furthermore, developments in the Middle East represent a humanitarian disaster with security and defense policy implications that threaten fundamental democratic values

[128] NATO remains the cornerstone of Norwegian security policy

[129] Burden-sharing considerations in NATO, as well as economic development in many allied countries, indicate that expectations for Norway will be greater, both to take greater responsibility for its own security and as a contributor to the alliance's defense

[130] Given the changes in Norway's strategic environment, there is a need to strengthen defense capabilities

[131] The development of security policy entails an increased need to improve the real ability of the Armed Forces to solve its tasks

[132] Should Norway or our allies be exposed to pressure, attacks or attacks, the Armed Forces must be able to react quickly and with relevant means

[133] In an unpredictable world, it is central that the Armed Forces are further developed as a preventive security policy instrument

[134] The Norwegian defense must, together with allied capacities, be a deterrent and be able to defend Norwegian and allied territory

[135] This means that Norway, within the framework of NATO, must have relevant and sufficient means of power which can counteract and deter pressure, aggression or attacks

[136] In order to ensure that Norway has a defense that can deal with changing challenges in the everpresent threat picture, a continuing willingness to invest in the Defense through adequate, stable and predictable framework conditions is required, combined with a willingness to constantly innovate and continue to improve efficiency internally in the sector

[137] The defense for an intervention defense was necessary and correct, and has given Norway a modern defense of high quality

[138] At the same time, there are individual financial challenges in the defense sector

[139] The reasons for these challenges are multiple and complex

[140] Some are due to external factors and changed assumptions that the sector itself can influence to a small extent, for example currency fluctuations and fuel prices

[141] Furthermore, a number of internal priorities and choices have been made over time, which have affected the freedom of action

[142] Overall, this is about a balance between maintaining the level of activity, preparedness and renewal

[143] In a situation where tasks, structure and organization have been developing, the activity dimension has been prioritized while less attention has been paid to logistics readiness

[144] However, the ability to deal with crisis and war in our immediate areas and with our allies at short notice must be given higher priority by strengthening the ability to be present, move around, react and persevere

[145] The development of security policy and long-term economic challenges in the defense sector means that there is a need to look at the balance between the tasks again

[146] The defense must be prepared to solve today and in the future, and the long-term financial framework for the defense sector

[147] The government will present a new long-term plan for the defense sector to the Storting in spring

[148] Following up the fighter aircraft acquisition with a base solution will constitute a main priority in 2016, in the next planning period and in the time beyond this

[149] This investment is of decisive importance for Norway's security and defence, and has major consequences for the defense structure and the defense economy

[150] In light of the changed security policy situation, the government prioritizes in 2016 to strengthen the monitoring, presence and assertion of sovereignty in the northern areas through a significant strengthening of the Intelligence Service, the Navy and the Air Force

[151] In the budget proposal, the government also prioritizes continuing

[152] Norway's contribution to the EU's operation to combat the humanitarian crisis in the Mediterranean and increase Norway's contribution to the UN operation in Mali (MINUSMA

[154] in the defense sector

[155] Current long-term plan The Storting went through the processing of the current long-term plan, ref. Storting's processing of Inst

[156] S (2011–2012) to Prop

[157] agreement that the Armed Forces must contribute to fulfilling the following defense policy objectives: –

[158] Alone and together with allies, secure Norwegian sovereignty, Norwegian rights, interests and values, as well as preserve Norwegian freedom of action against military and other pressure. – Through participation in multinational peace operations with unequivocal anchoring in the UN Charter and international defense cooperation, contribute to peace, stability, enforcement of international law and respect for human rights, as well as prevent the use of force by states and non-state actors against Norwegian and international security

[159] Together with allies, contribute to the collective defense of Norway and other allies in accordance with our alliance obligations, and to meet various types of attacks and attacks to ensure Norwegian and collective security. –

[160] Contribute to safeguarding Norwegian social security

[161] save lives and limit the consequences of accidents, disasters, attacks and attacks by governmental and non-governmental actors

[162] The tasks of the defense are an operationalization of the defense policy objectives

[163] These tasks can be summarized under the following headings

[164] a war-preventing threshold based on NATO membership. - Defend Norway and allies against serious threats, attacks and attacks, within the framework of NATO's collective defence. – Prevent and handle incidents and security policy crises with national resources, including facilitating allied engagement if necessary. – Ensure a national decision-making basis through timely monitoring and intelligence

[165] Claimed Norwegian sovereignty and sovereign rights

[166] Ensure the exercise of authority in demarcated areas. – Participate in multinational crisis management, including peace support operations

[167] Contribute to international cooperation in the field of defense and security policy

[168] for safeguarding social security and other key social tasks

[169] The ability of the defense to solve its tasks alone and together with allies has a deterrent effect in that the costs of threatening or attacking Norwegian security, Norwegian territory or Norwegian interests become unacceptably high

[170] The ability to handle military challenges must contribute to the challenges not arising

[171] The cornerstone of Norwegian security and defense policy is NATO membership

[172] Right from its establishment, NATO's main purpose has been to prevent war and conflict through a deterrent ability and willingness to collective defense if necessary

[173] NATO is also a collective framework for bilateral and multinational cooperation

[174] It is central that Norway actively contributes to NATO's deterrence appearing credible in our immediate areas as well

[175] Collective defense of Norway and allies will take place within the framework of NATO

[176] The defense must, together with our allies, deal with threats, attacks and attacks against

[177] Norway and other parts of NATO within the framework of NATO's collective defence

[178] The northern areas are Norway's most important strategic area of responsibility

[179] The collective defense obligation is mutual

[180] The defense must therefore also be able to make relevant contributions to the defense of other allies, based on key national capabilities

[181] The ability to contribute with Norwegian forces in collective defense in other parts of NATO is primarily developed based on the ability to handle crises, attacks and attacks at home

[182] The armed forces must be able to handle minor security policy crises themselves

[183] Episodes and crises that are handled nationally must be able to be brought under control quickly and with a minimum of negative consequences, possibly in parallel with the Norwegian authorities involving the alliance

[184] Although major military challenges must be handled with allied reinforcements, the Norwegian Armed Forces will have to independently meet threats and attacks in a relevant way, even before allies are involved

[185] A central objective will nevertheless be to facilitate allied involvement at an early stage

[186] The armed forces play an important aid role for society's overall preparedness

[187] The armed forces have many capacities which can make significant contributions in other crisis situations, for example in the case of accidents, natural disasters or terrorism

[188] The armed forces' capacities are available for national crisis management if civil authorities request assistance, and the best possible cooperation must be ensured between the armed forces, the police and other civil emergency authorities

[189] A crisis can affect several parts of society

[190] It can challenge the nation's ability for cross-sectoral crisis management

[191] Quick and correct strategic decisions are absolutely necessary for effective utilization of the Armed Forces' ability to avert, and deal with, episodes and security policy crises

[192] The long-term plans indicate and anchor main lines for the sector's development, including

[193] defense policy goals, tasks and level of ambition, as well as associated financial and structural frameworks

[194] This is based on an updated assessment of security policy, defense policy, economic and social conditions of importance for the development of the Armed Forces and the defense sector

[195] The long-term plans are based on updated strategic analyzes which clarify challenges and opportunities for the defense of Norway in the medium and longer term

[196] There have been extensive security policy changes since the previous plan was adopted, which actualize the challenges that have arisen over time in the Armed Forces

[197] It is therefore important to have a broad and timely review of what implications this should have for the organization of the Armed Forces going forward

[198] The competence- and technology-intensive activities of the armed forces require a long-term perspective in the development of structure and tasks

[199] This requires holistic thinking, and a long-term plan is a suitable tool to contribute to broad political anchoring of main priorities and choices

[200] The government will present a new long-term plan for the defense sector to the Storting in spring

[201] The long-term economic forecasts for the defense sector show that the economic challenges will persist and intensify if significant changes are not made

[202] In addition to this, there is a need to strengthen the Armed Forces as a result of security policy developments

[203] In the budget for 2016, the government proposes several increases in funding which are aimed at some of these challenges

[204] In working with the new long-term plan, it will nevertheless be necessary to assess increased frameworks, streamlining of staff and support functions and structural changes

[205] The Chief of Defense is, by virtue of his instructions, the highest professional military advisor in the Ministry of Defense and must promote independent professional military councils

[206] The Chief of Defense has therefore submitted his specialist military advice on how the identified challenges should be met, and a recommendation for further development of the Armed Forces

[207] This is a very central input in the preparation of a new long-term plan

[208] The director of the National Security Authority was tasked with assessing trends and developments within personnel, information and object security, and has, on this basis, proposed measures to improve preventive security

[209] Furthermore, the Ministry of Defense set up an independent expert group to provide input into the debate on the Defence's prerequisites to be able to solve its most demanding challenges should a security policy crisis and war arise

[210] Independent work has also been carried out by the consulting company McKinsey & Company to look for opportunities for further streamlining the sector

[211] The main findings and recommendations will also constitute important input in the work on the new long-term plan for the defense sector

[224] Social security and civil-military

[225] cooperation A main task for the Armed Forces is to assert Norway's sovereignty and, as part of the alliance defence, contribute to defending the country against external attack or political and military pressure

[226] The defense is therefore primarily a tool for military preparedness and military defence

[227] If civil society security is threatened in such a way that the police or other civil authorities alone are not able to handle the situation, these authorities can request the Armed Forces for assistance

[228] The ability of the armed forces to solve its tasks within state security depends to a considerable extent on a robust and well-functioning civil society

[229] In order to solve its main tasks, the Armed Forces also depend on arrangements that ensure necessary and safe access to civilian resources

[230] This is consistent with the total defense concept

[231] The defense sector has a number of capacities which, on request, can assist in civilian crisis situations, both in the event of accidents, natural disasters and serious criminal acts, including terrorist actions

[232] All of the Armed Forces' available resources can basically be called upon to safeguard civil society's security

[233] The restructuring and modernization of the defense sector has strengthened the Armed Forces' ability to quickly respond to both national and international operations and, in addition, the ability to provide assistance for social security with available resources

[234] In the time since the terrorist acts on 22 July 2011, emphasis has been placed on the fact that both civilian and military resources can be deployed quickly and effectively in serious crises

[235] As part of this, there has been a particular focus on further development and strengthening of the Armed Forces' preparedness to assist the police in dealing with terrorist situations

[236] The Ministry of Defense and the Ministry of Justice and Emergency Preparedness

[237] together reviewed the need to update civil-military arrangements and mechanisms within the total defense and in April 2015 published “Support and cooperation”, a description of the total defense today

[238] The purpose of this reference work is to contribute to anchoring the current total defense concept in the civil and military sector

[239] At the same time, the description of current arrangements and mechanisms will form an important part of the basis for further developing total defence

[240] Most schemes are essentially still comprehensive

[241] However, a need for updates has been identified, particularly in arrangements linked to security policy crisis and war

[277] The digital space The threat to society's ICT systems, as a result of targeted attacks, is large and increasing, and the methods are becoming more and more advanced

[278] This also applies to the threats against the defense sector's systems

[279] More and more sensitive information is stored in the digital space

[280] The modern network-based defense involves the use of information technology to link capacities and actors together in networks

[281] In many of today's conflicts, operations against ICT systems are used as means of action, along with other more traditional measures

[282] In 2016, emphasis will be placed on further developing the defense sector's work to reduce vulnerabilities in the digital space

[283] It is crucial that the defense sector has the necessary freedom of action in the digital space to support task solving at home and abroad

[284] The ability to defend in the digital space must be sufficient to meet the challenges

[285] The defense sector must be able to maintain the operation of ICT systems that are critical to the core business, including during crises and armed conflict

[286] There must therefore be sufficient preparedness to prevent failure of external systems from having serious, negative consequences for the defense sector

[287] Failures in civil ICT systems must, according to the principle of responsibility, be handled by the system owners and civil authorities

[288] Handling criminal acts in the digital space is a police responsibility

[289] Upon request, the Defense Forces will be able to provide support with available resources in this area

[290] The assistance follows the same principles as for other military assistance for civil society security

[291] In a situation with the risk of extensive cyber-attacks against critical infrastructure, the Armed Forces' resources will have to be prioritized to ensure the security of its own ICT systems

[292] The further development of NSM as the national professional environment for ICT security continues in

[293] NSM must contribute to better ICT security in society, and to meet the development of an increasingly complex ICT risk picture

[294] Civilian support for the Armed Forces In a serious crisis situation and in armed conflict, the Armed Forces' need for civilian support in the form of goods, services and access to infrastructure will exceed what the Armed Forces dispose of on a daily basis

[295] Civilian support is absolutely necessary to be able to maintain and further develop a relevant defense capability within a realistic financial framework

[296] Civil support for the Armed Forces must be based to the greatest extent possible on commercial agreements, if necessary with contingency clauses

[297] A good example of this is that in 2015 the Norwegian Armed Forces entered into an agreement with Wilhelmsen

[298] The Wilhelmsen group on deliveries of logistics services

[301] Among other things, the armed forces will need road, rail, sea and air transport for the transport of personnel, material and supplies, as well as the evacuation of the wounded

[302] There will also be a need for fuel supply, and more specialized services such as maintenance and engineering services

[303] Furthermore, the Armed Forces will be completely dependent on civilian health services

[1816] The internal audit function in the defense sector

[1817] The Ministry of Defense has its own internal audit unit

[1818] The internal audit must contribute to the realization of the goals for the defense sector by evaluating and advising on business management, risk management and internal control

[1819] An overall task is to assess whether these elements are appropriate, sufficient and function as intended

[1820] In the "Instructions for financial and business management in the defense sector" of 8 May 2015, the Ministry of Defense has continued the requirement that all agencies must have an internal audit function

[1821] The practical solution has been that the Department of Defence's internal audit, in addition to auditing the entire sector, also provides internal audit services to the heads of department in Forsvarsbygg, the Defense Research Institute and the National Security Authority, following their own instructions from these three department heads

[1822] Furthermore, the Ministry of Defence's internal audit will deliver the internal audit function to the head of the new department responsible for materiel investments and materiel management in the defense sector, which is planned to be established on 1 January

[1850] Strengthening the UN's peace operations The UN's peace operations are one of the organization's most central and sought-after instruments for maintaining international peace and security

[1851] The UN's integrated operations coordinate military, humanitarian and development-oriented efforts to achieve the best possible results

[1852] The Nordic countries have a stated ambition for closer cooperation on aid and joint UN efforts, which will continue

[1853] In 2016, the Ministry of Defense will also contribute to the work to strengthen the UN's ability to plan and carry out peace operations

[1854] This is done, among other things, through the special committee for peacekeeping operations, through support for the UN's work to improve the training of uniformed personnel and through participation in the preparation of uniform standards for task solving

[1855] Together with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Defense has also contributed input to the high-level panel set up by the UN Secretary-General, which was tasked with promoting proposals for how the UN can strengthen its operations

[1856] The report was submitted in the summer of 2015, and it is in line with Norwegian positions

[1857] Efforts will be made actively to nominate well-qualified personnel for leading positions in the UN, both for headquarters and for operations

[1858] Security sector reform in the defense sector Security sector reform (SSR) in the defense sector includes a wide range of instruments to assist in the reform of military forces, including assisting the recipient countries in safeguarding their own security and exercising authority, as well as contributing to bringing military forces under civilian and democratic control

[1859] SSR is an important tool to ensure democratic development in young democracies, and to contribute to ensuring lasting peace in former conflict areas

[1860] Norwegian SSR support is a supplement to the military force contributions that Norway provides in various operations abroad

[1861] The support is coordinated with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs

[1862] Norway has taken the initiative to strengthen Nordic-Baltic capacity building in the defense sector through the Nordic Baltic Assistance Programme

[1863] The aim is to be able to provide a component that can be incorporated into multinational operations and programs and which can engage the recipient country in strengthening the ability to safeguard its own security

[1864] There is a great demand for such efforts in NATO and other international organizations. Norwegian contributions to the SSR are aimed, among other things, at NATO's partner countries, especially the countries in the Western Balkans, Ukraine and Georgia

[1865] The contributions help to strengthen these countries' own security, as well as to develop a stronger NATO by preparing potential nations for membership or partnership

[1866] Norway is seconding a person to the NATO liaison offices in Ukraine and Georgia

[1867] Together with the Nordic countries and African partners, the Ministry of Defense also supports the African Union in its efforts to manage crisis on the African continent

[1868] The purpose is to assist countries in East Africa to establish regional capacity for crisis management and peace operations

[1869] Norway also supports SSR aimed at the armed forces in Iraq and Mali, within the framework of US-led and EU-led programmes, respectively

[1870] Contributions within the aforementioned areas and countries will also continue in

[2320] The intelligence service The changed security picture places great and increasing demands on situation overview and understanding

[2321] Norway's ability to handle the unexpected must be strengthened

[2322] The government proposes to increase the allocation to the Intelligence Service (E-service) by DKK 370 million kroner to carry out a necessary technological and capacity modernization that will make the E-service better able to handle today's and future challenges

[2323] The need for an efficient and relevant E-service increases in line with greater uncertainty in our local areas

[2324] While the challenges mount, the defense budgets of many NATO nations continue to decline

[2325] Developments in the Middle East and North Africa are also disturbing

[2326] A number of states have very weak state control, which provides fertile ground and free areas for both criminal and terrorist organizations

[2327] The possibility of the spread of these in in Europe, including Norway, is real

[2328] An effective foreign intelligence service is therefore very important in the overall effort to secure Norwegian security and safeguard Norwegian interests

[2329] There is a need to strengthen the Eservice's technical, operational and personnel competence, also with regard to the technology available to current players

[2330] The ever-faster technological development entails significant challenges with the associated need for rapid support and a high rate of change in evernew fields

[2331] In 2016, the e-service will continue to prioritize following up developments in Russia and the northern regions

[2332] The Middle East and North Africa will also be given high priority

[2333] In addition, the E-service will prioritize following the development of international Islamist networks and the far-right environment in a Europe characterized by increasingly social and economic unrest

[2334] Developments in Ukraine and the Middle East, among others, will require increased attention

[2335] Intelligence support for Norwegian forces in international operations will also be a central task for the E-service in

[2336] In 2016, the E-service's new intelligence vessel, F/S Marjata, will be put into operation

[2337] This will provide a significant increase in capacity compared to the previous research vessel

[3158] It has long been a priority goal to reduce the completion time in material projects and increase the quality of material management

[3159] The establishment of a materiel agency for the defense sector must contribute to improving the portfolio and project management of materiel projects

[3200] Introductory part The government's climate and environmental policy is based on the fact that all sectors of society have an independent responsibility to base their activities on environmental considerations and to contribute to the achievement of the national climate and environmental policy goals

[3201] Furthermore, the sector governing bodies are responsible for implementing the measures needed to be able to achieve the goals in the climate and environmental policy

[3202] For a discussion of the government's overall climate- and environment-relevant matters, see the Department of Climate and Environment's professional proposal

[3203] The climate and environmental challenges of the defense sector are particularly linked to the fact that the use of equipment, training, exercises and operational activities can cause noise pollution, damage to nature and the environment and emissions of greenhouse gases

[3204] The defense sector's extensive building stock also entails a significant consumption of energy for operation and heating, which directly and indirectly results in the emission of greenhouse gases

[3205] The defense sector follows the national environmental policy and must take care of the sectoral responsibility in the environmental area

[3206] The agencies in the defense sector have an independent responsibility for finding good solutions and effective measures to reduce the burden on the environment

[3208] Central to the environmental management system is the commitment to continuous improvement of the environmental status

[3430] In addition, female employees are highlighted in the profiling of NSM in order to strengthen the business as an attractive workplace for both sexes

[3431] NSM also continues to seek to recruit even more competent women for technological positions

[3434] NSM seeks to facilitate people with reduced functional capacity, and implements necessary measures based on individual assessment

[3435] NSM also focuses on facilitating employees in different life stages. The Defense Research Institute The Defense Research Institute (FFI) arranges for the institute to have a composition of its employees that shows diversity in age, gender, ethnicity and functional ability

[3436] A targeted recruitment scheme, well-thought-out salary policy and raising awareness among managers are measures FFI uses to achieve this

[3437] It is a goal to increase the proportion of women in the groups where this proportion is low

[3445] The scientific business is technology-heavy, and FFI recruits from subjects that are dominated by men

[3446] The recruitment policy is active and targeted, and FFI emphasizes recruiting more women, especially for scientific positions

[3447] The institute has succeeded in this, and the number of women in scientific positions has increased steadily since 2004, but in 2014 there was a slight decrease for the first time

[3453] of the applicant pool, an increase of three percentage points

[3473] Ministry of Defence NATO's assessment of Norway - performance measurement. In addition to the more comprehensive assessments of the individual nation's defense plans and defense efforts, measurement systems have been developed in NATO which make visible the contribution of the member states within selected areas

[3474] The measurement gives an indication of how the nations have used their resources and strengths

[3475] In addition, an assessment is given of how large a number of the forces are available for, and which can be maintained over time, in international operations

[3476] It is challenging to establish systems in NATO that can comprehensively and comprehensively measure the nations' total contributions, and not least the quality of the contributions

[3477] The measurements therefore only provide a simplified quantitative presentation of the nations' contribution in individual areas, and are a supplement to

[3478] the more thorough and holistic assessments

[3479] Below follows a fact sheet for Norway which lists the various indicators in the measurement and which illustrates how Norway is positioned in relation to NATO's other member states

[3480] The indicators are based on accounting figures and not on balanced budgets

[3481] Overall, Norway comes out well in this measurement

[3579] The Storting agrees that the Ministry of Defense can in 2016: dispose of real estate

[3580] regardless of value at market price when there is no other state need for the property

[3581] The properties must normally be put up for sale on the market, but can be sold directly to county councils or municipalities at market price, within the provisions of the EEA Agreement

[3582] If the properties are currently for outdoor or cultural purposes, they can be sold on the same terms to Statskog SF if no county councils or municipalities want to buy the properties

[3583] Likewise, properties that are necessary to fulfill society's objective of maintaining a self-financed civil aviation can be sold directly to Avinor AS

[3584] This applies to the following property categories: runways, taxiways with associated safety areas, aircraft stands and other areas and infrastructure for flight operations, terminals designed to meet the service and service needs of consumers and authorities, areas for collective and private passenger services, offices and similar properties for future development, disposal of real estate for a value of up to DKK 100,000 free of charge or at a reduced price when special reasons exist. IX Time of loading of expenditure allocations

[3585] The Storting agrees that in 2016 the Ministry of Defense can charge spending allocations for orders through NSPA (NATO Support Agency), other international organizations or other country’s authorities from the time the material is ordered, even if delivery does not take place until later in the budget year or in a subsequent budget year

[3586] The following provides an overview of the provisions that apply to conscription in

[3587] First-time service Distribution for first-time service must be based on fair and as equal as possible treatment of conscripts and volunteers

[3588] The wishes of the individual must be emphasized and everyone must have the same opportunity to compete for service positions

[3589] The duration of the initial service is normally twelve months

[3590] but can be differentiated between six and 18 months

[3591] The armed forces can shorten the service by up to six weeks

[3592] For reasons of education and work, the individual conscript who has been called up for a minimum of twelve months' service can be discharged early up to six weeks before the normal discharge date

[3593] The service time reductions must be carried out in a way that provides predictability for the conscripts and does not have consequences for readiness or weaken the recruitment basis for operations abroad

[3594] Crews who do not want to reduce their service time can be given the opportunity to complete the service if the conditions are right for it

[3595] Special arrangements Conscripts and conscription crews serving their first service can take up to six weeks of the parental allowance period

[3596] This is in addition to 14 days leave in connection with the birth of your own child

[3597] Joint provisions The joint upper limit for total ordinary duty is 19 months or 575 days

[3598] Voluntary service in the Home Guard's task force or in operations abroad is not considered part of the ordinary duty. Repetition and auxiliary service and course Auxiliary service in connection with repetition service and etterutdanning course can be called into service or conscripts who are not assigned to a military department or the joint institutions of the Armed Forces. Repetition and auxiliary service for conscripts and conscript crews is normally 21 days

[3599] Conscripted and discharged commanders and specialists can also be called into service nine days before or after each exercise

[3600] Such service must not exceed 36 days

[3601] Invitations for repetition and help service as well as courses must be made within the framework of the total number of days set for such service

[3602] There is no limit to the number of call-ups during the compulsory service period

[3603] A minimum of two years must normally elapse between the end of initial service and repetition or auxiliary service, and between each repetition or auxiliary service

[3604] More frequent call-ups to duty must preferably take place on a voluntary basis. Conscription and conscripted personnel (commanders and privates) who are assigned to staffs or departments and who are required to train or educate each year, may be called up for short refresher service or a course each year

[3605] Conscripted and discharged

[3606] commanders can be summoned to a refresher course of up to twelve days' duration

[3607] The army can call in conscripted and discharged commanders who say they are willing to command positions and pre-determined key positions at lower and middle level for a further training course of up to five weeks duration

[3608] Conscript academic officers and students in the subjects of pharmacy, law, medicine, theology, psychology, odontology and veterinary medicine, who have completed twelve months' initial service, can be called up for 90 days' service at staff or in a department

[3609] Players can alternatively serve with forces abroad where Norway participates. Conscription and service-obligatory personnel who are granted a postponement of their service can be called up to serve the rest of their service at other departments in the Armed Forces and, if necessary, in another budget year

[3610] In addition to the rehearsal and support service, conscripts and discharged officers, private specialists and special professional groups can for a small part of 158 Prop

[3611] S 2015–2016 Ministry of Defense the individual department's organizational plan is given up to ten days' service

[3612] The Home Guard service In the Home Guard, the annual duty is up to six days for corporals and privates and up to nine days for officers and specialists

[3613] The task force is voluntary personnel on a three-year contract, and has up to 30 days of annual duty in addition to the general duty in Heimevernet

[3614] Duty of service for women

[3615] who voluntarily serve in the Armed Forces today have a duty of disposition and service

[3616] They assume the same obligations as conscripted men when they have signed a contract of service for female military personnel

[3623] The same applies to the women who are already serving in the Armed Forces
